chapter: Church funerals, band size and mourning
title: Cigar-box collections to hire a funeral band
summary: Mac and Parker explain bands hired by passing the cigar box for a well-known man.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Years ago, that's all every male, every student that had was banned. If they didn't have the loan around the vicinity, they passed the sickle box around and collect enough money to buy, to hire the band they had in order for the second line. And they buried him. Oh, they'd pick up enough money. Pick up enough money to hire the band.
Hire a band. That's without a club at all, huh?
Without a club, no. He had to be, you know, well-known. Well-known, that's all.
So-and-so, they had to eat, don't belong to nothing, give me a cigar box. This fella get one, that fella get one. Go around all the ballrooms, everywhere.
Pick up enough money. Sometimes they have two bands, those are what they pick up.
We saw that in Wagaman with the cigar box. Joe Avery's son was out there with the cigar box.
You remember Joe Avery, the tri-ball player?
